name: web/threejs-page
title: three.js page by hand
summary: Write one HTML file with a hand-written three.js page: CDN import map, renderer, scene, camera, light, objects, animation loop and resize handler.
when: Use when no kit fits and the page needs three.js written by hand: its own shapes, shaders or layout of objects.
steps: Match the requested filename, style, and assets. Keep the page as one HTML file if requested. A pinned three.js CDN needs connectivity; for offline Three.js, inline a local bundle. For an HTTP project, use local modules and serve their folder.

Model the requested subject with named groups and pivots at its joints. For a real mechanism, verify the geometry and direction of motion or label the depiction as illustrative. Keep the camera stable and frame the whole path on desktop and phone.
Define the action in timed phases and advance the subject itself. Add replay or pause when appropriate. Sound starts on a user gesture. Use fallbacks for missing imports, assets, and WebGL.

Use look_at_page to inspect the requested filename and repair observed issues. Check several subject poses or the full action, including the intended final pose. Camera changes and running callbacks are weak evidence for subject motion.
next: Report the filename and which states were verified.
